quotes.text: If you remember nothing else, Co-pilot is your inbox partner. Rag is your knowledge pipeline. Use the guide when you're inside the district. Build the pipeline when the stakes demand proof.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's decision rule between Copilot and RAG into one memorable contrast.

quotes.text: Rag isn't about shoving PDFs into a hungry mouth. It's a supply chain. Data in. Chunks clean. Index is tuned. Queries tight. Evaluation constant. Break any link. And the outputs rot.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames RAG as an end-to-end data supply chain rather than a model feature.

quotes.text: Trust isn't about personality, it's about auditability, mandatory citations make every response traceable, it also makes QA measurable, you can test retrieval
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why mandatory citations are the basis of trust and quality assurance.

quotes.text: Rag is not a feature you toggle on Tuesdays. It's a discipline, sources owned, pipelines monitored, evaluations weekly, users in the loop
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation that RAG needs ongoing operational ownership.

takeaways: Microsoft 365 Copilot is the right tool for drafts, summaries and quick lookups inside Microsoft 365, within the user's existing permissions.
When answers depend on proprietary data outside Microsoft 365 or must be cited and repeatable, a RAG pipeline with chunking, embeddings and Azure AI Search is needed.
RAG quality comes from data discipline - metadata, re-indexing, mandatory citations, don't-know behavior and continuous evaluation - not from retraining the model.
hook: Many teams expect Microsoft 365 Copilot to know policies and SOPs it cannot see, and then pay in rework and lost trust. This episode helps IT and AI leads decide when Copilot is enough and when they need their own retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. It walks through how RAG works in Azure and a manufacturing case study that cut service desk load.
